title: PIMA workflows
text: direct input pima() named list fitted models. use package’s Pima Indians diabetes data test coefficient number pregnancies across logistic regressions. main arguments : mods: list model objects, usually glm objects. tested_coeffs: coefficients test. can character vector common models, list one character vector per model. n_flips: number sign flips. method: multiplicity adjustment, "maxT", "minP", "none". score_type, seed, output_models, arguments passed flipscores::flipscores(). conceptual effect different coefficient names across models, use list tested_coeffs.
code: data("pimads")  pima_data <- na.omit(pimads) pima_data$diabetes01 <- as.integer(pima_data$diabetes == "pos")  mods <- list(   full = glm(     diabetes01 ~ npreg + glucose + pressure + bmi + age,     data = pima_data,     family = binomial()   ),   compact = glm(     diabetes01 ~ npreg + glucose + bmi,     data = pima_data,     family = binomial()   ),   sqrt_bmi = glm(     diabetes01 ~ npreg + glucose + sqrt(bmi) + age,     data = pima_data,     family = binomial()   ),   glucose_only = glm(     diabetes01 ~ npreg + glucose,     data = pima_data,     family = binomial()   ) )  manual_res <- pima(   mods,   tested_coeffs = "npreg",   n_flips = n_flips_vignette,   method = "maxT",   score_type = "standardized",   seed = 1 )  summary(manual_res, digits = 3) #>          model   response coefficient estimate   score     se     z  pcor     p #> 1      compact diabetes01       npreg    0.168 159.150 31.103 5.117 0.226 0.001 #> 2         full diabetes01       npreg    0.114  64.253 23.866 2.692 0.119 0.014 #> 3 glucose_only diabetes01       npreg    0.151 152.211 31.762 4.792 0.208 0.001 #> 4     sqrt_bmi diabetes01       npreg    0.113  64.283 23.988 2.680 0.119 0.014 #>   p.adj   family  link #> 1 0.001 binomial logit #> 2 0.014 binomial logit #> 3 0.001 binomial logit #> 4 0.014 binomial logit mods_mixed <- list(   linear = glm(     diabetes01 ~ npreg + glucose + bmi,     data = pima_data,     family = binomial()   ),   quadratic = glm(     diabetes01 ~ I(npreg^2) + glucose + bmi,     data = pima_data,     family = binomial()   ) )  mixed_res <- pima(   mods_mixed,   tested_coeffs = list(     linear = "npreg",     quadratic = "I(npreg^2)"   ),   n_flips = n_flips_vignette,   seed = 1 )  summary(mixed_res, digits = 3) #>       model   response coefficient estimate    score      se     z  pcor     p #> 1    linear diabetes01       npreg    0.168  159.150  31.103 5.117 0.226 0.001 #> 2 quadratic diabetes01  I(npreg^2)    0.015 1807.835 366.472 4.933 title: PIMA workflows
text: models supplied manually, pima() tries reconstruct formula decisions fitted models. can add scenario-level metadata extra; useful plotting grouping analytical decisions.
code: extra <- data.frame(   model = names(mods),   adjustment = c("full", "compact", "sqrt_bmi", "minimal"),   includes_age = c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE) )  manual_res <- pima(   mods,   tested_coeffs = "npreg",   n_flips = n_flips_vignette,   seed = 1,   extra = extra )  manual_res #>  #> == Multiverse analysis with 4 scenarios == #>  #>          model                                             formula   family #> 1      compact                  diabetes01 ~ npreg + glucose + bmi binomial #> 2         full diabetes01 ~ npreg + glucose + pressure + bmi + age binomial #> 3 glucose_only                        diabetes01 ~ npreg + glucose binomial #> 4     sqrt_bmi      diabetes01 ~ npreg + glucose + sqrt(bmi) + age binomial #>    link   Intercept npreg glucose pressure       bmi  age adjustment #> 1 logit (Intercept) npreg glucose     <NA>       bmi <NA>    compact #> 2 logit (Intercept) npreg glucose pressure       bmi  age       full #> 3 logit (Intercept) npreg glucose     <NA>      <NA> <NA>    minimal #> 4 logit (Intercept) npreg glucose     <NA> sqrt(bmi)  age   sqrt_bmi #>   includes_age #> 1        FALSE #> 2         TRUE #> 3        FALSE #> 4         TRUE

title: PIMA workflows
text: plot() creates volcano-style view: estimate-like quantity x-axis raw adjusted p-values y-axis. p-value transformation can "z", "-log10", "raw", custom function.  plot can tuned arguments users usually need practice: xvar: numeric column summary(res), example "estimate", "pcor", "score" "z"; p.adjusted: TRUE adjusted p-values, FALSE raw p-values; p.transf: "z", "-log10", "raw" custom function; : grouping variable, including metadata supplied extra; facet, facet.scales, shapes, alpha, xlab, ylab.  Regular expressions handy coefficient names generated transformations factor contrasts.  volcano() adds quantile reference lines p-value cutoffs top plotting idea.
code: plot(   manual_res,   focal = "npreg",   xvar = "estimate",   p.adjusted = TRUE,   p.transf = "-log10" ) plot(   manual_res,   by = "adjustment",   xvar = "pcor",   p.adjusted = FALSE,   p.transf = "z",   alpha = 0.05,   shapes = c(1, 16),   xlab = "Partial correlation",   ylab = "Raw p-value, z scale" ) plot(   mixed_res,   focal = "npreg",   regex = TRUE,   xvar = "estimate",   p.adjusted = FALSE,   p.transf = "raw",   alpha = 0.10,   facet.scales = "free" ) volcano(   manual_res,   focal = "npreg",   p.adjusted = FALSE,   p.cut = c(0.10, 0.05, 0.01),   q = c(0.10, 0.50, 0.90) )

title: PIMA workflows
text: spec_curve() combines two panels: top panel shows result specification, bottom panel shows analytical decisions generated specification.  test several coefficients several responses, spec_curve() can facet result.
code: spec_curve(   manual_res,   focal = "npreg",   yvar = "estimate",   p.adjusted = TRUE,   alpha = 0.05,   tbr = c(0.55, 0.45),   colors = c("grey45", "#0072B2"),   shapes = c(1, 16),   title = "Manual multiverse: coefficient estimates",   xlab = "Model specification",   ylab = "Log-odds estimate",   top.theme = spec_top_theme,   bottom.theme = spec_bottom_theme,   conf.int = TRUE,   redundant = FALSE ) set.seed(123) n <- 30 sim_data <- data.frame(   x = rnorm(n),   z1 = rnorm(n),   z2 = rnorm(n) ) sim_data$y1 <- sim_data$x + sim_data$z1 + rnorm(n) sim_data$y2 <- sim_data$x + sim_data$z2 + rnorm(n)  sim_mods <- list(   y1_linear = glm(y1 ~ x + z1 + z2, data = sim_data),   y1_poly = glm(y1 ~ x + poly(z1, 2) + z2, data = sim_data),   y2_linear = glm(y2 ~ x + z1 + z2, data = sim_data),   y2_poly = glm(y2 ~ x + z1 + poly(z2, 2), data = sim_data) )  sim_res <- pima(   sim_mods,   tested_coeffs = "x",   n_flips = n_flips_vignette,   seed = 1 )  plot(sim_res, facet = response ~ ., p.adjusted = FALSE) spec_curve(   sim_res,   focal = "x",   p.adjusted = FALSE,   facet.y = TRUE,   tbr = c(0.60, 0.40),   which.response = c("y1", "y2"),   title = "Two responses, one focal coefficient",   top.theme = spec_top_theme,   bottom.theme = spec_bottom_theme,   redundant = FALSE )

title: PIMA workflows
text: create_multi() builds scenario grid . crosses: predictor inclusion transformations; optional row subsets; optional fitting specifications. right-hand side formula must contain bare additive predictors. Put transformations nfuns cfuns, directly inside formula. spec_<variable> columns record analytical choice predictor: "excluded", "identity", transformation name. Models fitted fit.specs supplied. Failed fits kept error objects marked scenarios$fit_ok, usually convenient subset calling pima(). metadata create_multi() carried pima result. large grid, scatter plot useful overview.  full specification curve one hundred scenarios usually dense vignette page. good reporting pattern show complete overview draw focused curves meaningful slices multiverse.  really want inspect every scenario, export complete curve standalone SVG/PDF instead forcing vignette body. code evaluated 108-scenario curve dense inline reading. transf.focal = TRUE allows transformations focal predictors . useful focal effect can parameterized multiple ways.

text: pima() also experimental support objects multiverse package. key convention universe must create fitted model called fit. example uses hurricane data shipped multiverse, hurricane data shipped pima. branches declared multiverse::branch() stored metadata can used grouping specification curves.
code: library(multiverse)  data("hurricane", package = "multiverse")  hurricane_mv <- transform(   hurricane,   log_NDAM = log(NDAM + 1) )  M <- multiverse()  inside(M, {   fit <- glm(     alldeaths ~       MasFem +       branch(         pressure,         "original" ~ MinPressure_before,         "updated" ~ Minpressure_Updated_2014       ) +       branch(         damage,         "raw" ~ NDAM,         "logged" ~ log_NDAM       ),     data = hurricane_mv,     family = quasipoisson()   ) })  execute_multiverse(M)  parameters(M) #> $pressure #> $pressure[[1]] #> [1] "original" #>  #> $pressure[[2]] #> [1] "updated" #>  #>  #> $damage #> $damage[[1]] #> [1] "raw" #>  #> $damage[[2]] #> [1] "logged"  hurricane_res <- pima(   M,   tested_coeffs = "MasFem",   n_flips = n_flips_vignette,   seed = 1 )  summary(hurricane_res, digits = 3) #>   model  response coefficient estimate    score       se     z  pcor     p #> 1  mod1 alldeaths      MasFem    0.145 3106.494 1672.095 1.858 0.195 0.107 #> 2  mod2 alldeaths      MasFem    0.211 4889.632 1918.654 2.548 0.267 0.059 #> 3  mod3 alldeaths      MasFem    0.141 2963.215 1653.939 1.792 0.188 0.142 #> 4  mod4 alldeaths      MasFem    0.204 4518.155 1850.998 2.441 0.256 0.079 #>   p.adj pressure damage       family link #> 1 0.200 original    raw quasipoisson  log #> 2 0.069 original logged quasipoisson  log #> 3 0.200  updated    raw quasipoisson  log #> 4 0.081  updated logged quasipoisson  log plot(   hurricane_res,   by = c("pressure", "damage"),   xvar = "estimate",   p.transf = "-log10",   p.adjusted = FALSE ) spec_curve(   hurricane_res,   focal = "MasFem",   p.adjusted = FALSE,   tbr = c(0.60, 0.40),   colors = c("grey55", "#009E73"),   title = "Hurricane multiverse from the multiverse package",   top.theme = spec_top_theme,   bottom.theme = spec_bottom_theme,   redundant = FALSE )

text: pima() applies multiplicity adjustment main call method = "maxT" method = "minP". can also compute raw p-values first method = "none" call p.adjust() later. next example uses factor predictor, also lets us show combine_contrasts(). raw_factor_res computed method = "none", contains raw p-values . re-exported p.adjust() function adds adjusted p-values joint resampling distribution. combine_tests() answers global questions combining test statistics. argument, asks whether least one tested effect present anywhere multiverse. = "model" = "coefficient", asks question within model coefficient. can also define custom groups by_list. list elements can contain test positions, column names Tspace, want groups correspond single metadata column. combine_contrasts() combines contrasts factor variables one global test factor. example groupB groupC become single group test within model.
